name: Ask customers for an NPS score on WhatsApp after a purchase with Turbo Notify

nodes.name: Receive an order
nodes.notes: Needs Header Auth: a request without the right header is refused and never reaches the workflow. After an import check the Production URL shown in this node: that is the address to call. An import through the API or the CLI keeps the path of the file: change it to a new random value. Never shorten it. Share the Production URL and the header value only with your shop or booking system, over HTTPS.

nodes.name: Poll WhatsApp replies
nodes.notes: Reads the replies of your customers every 5 minutes. Works on every plan. On n8n Cloud each poll that finds a message counts as an execution: make it slower on a small plan. A reply written while n8n was off is read at the next poll, while its text still exists.

nodes.name: Every 30 minutes: ask the surveys that are due
nodes.notes: Every 30 minutes (about 1,440 executions a month on n8n Cloud) it asks the surveys that are due, inside your sending hours, and closes the ones nobody answered. To spend fewer, use a Cron expression limited to your sending hours.

nodes.name: Every week: send the NPS report
nodes.notes: Monday at 8:00 (in the workflow time zone) it sends you the NPS report of the last 7 days.

assignments.name: optout_words
assignments.value: stop, parar, sair, pare, cancelar, descadastrar, unsubscribe, para

assignments.name: msg_question
assignments.value: Hi {name}, thanks for your order {order_id} at {business}. From 0 to 10, how likely are you to recommend us to a friend? Reply with a number (you may add one sentence). To stop these questions, reply STOP.

assignments.name: msg_reask
assignments.value: Sorry, I did not catch that. Please reply with a number from 0 to 10, or STOP to stop these questions.

assignments.name: msg_promoter
assignments.value: Thank you, {name}! We are glad you had a good experience.

assignments.name: msg_review_invite
assignments.value: If you have a minute, a public review helps other people find us.

assignments.name: msg_passive
assignments.value: Thank you, {name}. What would make it a 10 for you?

assignments.name: msg_detractor
assignments.value: I am sorry, {name}. What went wrong? A person will read your answer.

assignments.name: msg_comment_thanks
assignments.value: Thank you, {name}. Your answer reached us.

assignments.name: msg_optout_confirm
assignments.value: Done. We will not ask you again.

assignments.name: msg_report

nodes.name: Your settings
nodes.notes:
owner_phone: your own WhatsApp number, with + and the country code. It gets the alert about an unhappy customer and the weekly report, at any hour (these alerts are not held back by the sending hours). It must be a different phone from the number linked to Turbo Notify: messages to yourself have no push. It counts as one of the 2 contacts per cycle on Free. Replace it: the workflow stops while it is a placeholder
business_name: how the texts name your business ({business}). Replace it: the workflow stops while it is the sample
number_alias: the number that sends the questions and reads the replies: main, or the alias or the num_ id of an extra number. Replies written to another number of the account are ignored. Also set Options > Number on the Polling Trigger to save reads
review_url: the page where a customer is sent to leave a public review (your Google Maps or Trustpilot link). Empty: nobody gets a review button
review_button_text: text on the review button, at most 20 characters
review_for: who gets the review link when review_url is set. everyone: every customer who answered with a score (the link comes with the last thanks, so a customer who writes no comment is not sent one). promoters: only a 9 or 10. WARNING: asking only the happy customers for a review is selective solicitation. Review platforms such as Google prohibit it and consumer regulators can treat it as deceptive. This is not legal advice
expected_timezone: the time zone of your sending hours. The workflow time zone (Workflow settings, Timezone) must be the same, or the two timers stop. Orders and replies are never stopped by it
default_country_code: added to local phone numbers that come without +. Works for 55 (Brazil). With another code only numbers that start with it, or with +, are accepted: outside Brazil your shop must send numbers with + and the country code
start_statuses: the order statuses that start a survey, comma separated, or * for any status. Choose the status that means the customer HAS the product: a question 24 hours after payment can arrive before the parcel. The first matching event of an order starts the clock, a later one is ignored. A status that matches nothing leaves a row status-01 to status-20 in the table that says which status arrived
delay_hours: hours between the order event and the question. 0 asks at the next timer run
window_start: sending hours, start (24 hour clock, in expected_timezone). Nobody is asked before it
window_end: sending hours, end. Nobody is asked from this time on. A survey that falls outside waits for the next window
cooldown_days: one survey per customer per period: a customer asked in the last this many days is not asked about a new order. 0 switches it off
max_surveys_per_day: most questions sent per day (your local day). The rest wait for the next day. These are first messages to people who never wrote to the number, the kind WhatsApp users report: a new number may send only 50 messages on its first day, so start low
max_surveys_per_run: most questions sent in ONE run of the timer, so a backlog at the opening of the sending hours does not go out as one burst
close_after_days: days after which a question nobody answered (or a comment nobody wrote) is closed. A survey that could not be sent in time is skipped
purge_days: closed, skipped and failed rows older than this many days are deleted once a week, with the notes about statuses. 0 never deletes, otherwise 60 or more. A customer who opted out is never deleted: deleting that row would let the workflow ask them again
max_text_length: longest customer name and list of items kept. Longer text is cut. A name or list that carries a web address is dropped
max_comment_length: longest comment kept and forwarded. Longer text is cut
optout_words: a WHOLE message that stops the questions for that customer, comma separated. Capitals, accents and punctuation do not matter. A sentence that holds one ("please stop") does not match: it is an unclear answer and gets ONE re-ask that tells how to stop
name_fallback: what {name} becomes when the order has no customer name (pt-BR: cliente)
field_order_id: name of the field in your order that holds a unique order id (1 to 64 letters, digits or . _ # : -, not starting with report-, optout- or status-)
field_customer_name: name of the field with the customer name
field_phone: name of the field with the customer WhatsApp number
field_status: name of the field with the status of the order
field_order_url: name of the field with a link to the order, optional. It goes to you in the unhappy customer alert
field_items: name of the field with what was bought, optional. A list of names, a list of objects with name or title, or a text
msg_question: the question. {name} {order_id} {business} {items}. \n is a line break. Keep the STOP line (or the word you set in optout_words)
msg_reask: sent ONCE when the answer holds no clear number. After a second unclear answer the survey closes
msg_promoter: sent for a 9 or 10
msg_review_invite: added under the thanks, with the review button, only when review_url is set. Keep it neutral: it goes to everyone when review_for is everyone
msg_passive: sent for a 7 or 8. The next message of the customer is stored as the comment
msg_detractor: sent for a 0 to 6. The next message of the customer is stored as the comment and sent to you
msg_comment_thanks: the one short thanks after the comment is stored (with the review button when review_for is everyone)
msg_optout_confirm: confirms a STOP, once
msg_owner_alert: sent to you at once for a 0 to 6, followed by the customer contact card. {customer_name} {score} {order_id} {order_url} {items}. A line whose placeholder is empty is dropped
msg_owner_comment: sent to you with the comment of an unhappy customer
msg_report: the weekly report, sent to you. {days} {asked} {answered} {rate} {nps} {promoters} {passives} {detractors} {comments} {failed} {skipped}

nodes.name: Check the settings
nodes.notes: Stops the run while a setting is a sample or makes no sense. For the two timers the time zone too (an order or a reply is never lost to it). Then it hands on what the trigger delivered.

nodes.name: Read the surveys
nodes.notes: Reads, once per run, the surveys that are waiting (queued, asked, answered), everyone who opted out, and everything created in the last 31 days (or cooldown_days, if longer).

nodes.name: Decide what to do
nodes.notes: A new order is checked and queued (or skipped, with the reason). A timer run closes old surveys and asks the due ones. The week run writes the report and clears old rows. A poll run picks the replies from customers who owe an answer.

nodes.name: Where does this go?
nodes.notes: Read the reply in full: a reply from a customer who owes an answer. Delete old rows: the weekly clean-up. Save a plan: everything else, ready to be saved.

nodes.name: Delete old rows (purge_days)
nodes.notes: Once a week, when purge_days is not 0: deletes closed, skipped and failed rows older than purge_days. Never a customer who opted out, never a survey that is still open.

nodes.name: Read the whole message
nodes.notes: The poll carries only the first 50 characters of a message. This reads the whole text, so a comment is stored and forwarded complete. Only replies of customers who owe an answer are read.

nodes.name: Decide about the replies
nodes.notes: Judges the replies one after the other: a score, a re-ask, a comment, or STOP. Nothing else gets an answer.

nodes.name: Save the survey before sending
nodes.notes: The row is stored BEFORE anybody is messaged, so a restart cannot lose an order, an answer or an opt-out.

nodes.name: Write the messages
nodes.notes: The one place that makes every text, from the wording in Your settings. A row with nothing to send ends here.

nodes.name: Which kind of message?
nodes.notes: Text for the question, the thanks and the alerts. A link button for a happy customer. A contact card for the unhappy customer.

nodes.name: Send the text
nodes.notes: The question, the re-ask, the follow-ups, the thanks, the alerts to you and the report. A refused send never stops the others and the row records why.

nodes.name: Send the thank you with the review button
nodes.notes: One message: the thanks with a button that opens your review page.

nodes.name: Send the contact card to the owner
nodes.notes: The card of the unhappy customer, sent to you, so you can write back with one tap.

nodes.name: Gather the answers of Turbo Notify
nodes.notes: Puts the answers of the three send nodes back together.

nodes.name: Record the answers
nodes.notes: Matches each answer with its message and writes the message id, or the reason it was refused, into the row. A question that was refused makes the row send_failed.

nodes.name: Save the survey after sending
nodes.notes: Writes the message id of the question, or the failure, into the row.

nodes.name: Report what failed
nodes.notes: Fails the run when a message was refused, naming the order. This is what your Error workflow reacts to.

parameters.content:
### How it works
Your shop posts a JSON order event (order_id, phone, status, customer_name) to a protected webhook. A day after the status you choose (delivered by default) the customer gets one WhatsApp question, 0 to 10, inside your sending hours.

A 9 or 10 is thanked, a 7 or 8 is asked what would make it a 10, and a 0 to 6 is asked what went wrong while you get an alert with the contact card. STOP opts out. A weekly report gives the NPS. It is not a chatbot.

### Setup
1. Install [@turbo-notify/n8n-nodes-turbo-notify](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@turbo-notify/n8n-nodes-turbo-notify) (tested 1.5.15).
2. Create a Turbo Notify API credential (messages:send, messages:read, events:read) and a Header Auth credential "Order access (Header Auth)".
3. Run the manual branch once.
4. In Your settings type owner_phone (not the number linked to Turbo Notify) and business_name, then check start_statuses, time zone, hours and texts.
5. Activate, test with your own phone, then point your shop at the Production URL.

### Customization
Texts, delay, cooldown and caps are in Your settings. On a small n8n Cloud plan slow the timer and the poll down.

## Four ways in

An order from your shop, a reply, a timer every 30 minutes and a weekly timer.

## Check, then read the table

Stops on a sample setting, then reads the survey rows once.

## Decide what to do

Queue an order, ask what is due, report the week, clear old rows or judge a reply.

## Save, then write

The row is saved before anything is sent. Every text comes from your settings.

## Send

Text, review button or contact card. A refused send never stops the others.

## Record and report

The message id or the failure goes into the row. A refusal then fails the run.

## Run once: create the table

Creates surveys when missing. Safe to run again.
**Replace the samples before you activate.** While owner_phone or business_name is a sample, the workflow asks nobody.
